parent.title: claude-crew foundation
parent.body: Dependency-ordered foundation work, compiled from the capability catalog. Each child is unsafe to start before its blockers are done.

children.title: Extend Application / API Service Layer
children.why: A real seam exists: two dot-sourced libraries (_session-config.ps1, _session-brief.ps1) are loaded first by every entry script, so config resolution and brief generation are not duplicated per script. What is missing is a contract on that seam - there is no JSON schema for session-plugin.json and no schemaVersion field, so a config written for an older crew fails at whatever line first dereferences a missing key rather than at one validation boundary with a usable message. Open issue #9 pushes substantially more structure through this seam (templates, detected stacks, generated lanes), which makes the absent schema more load-bearing rather than less.

children.title: Extend Security
children.why: Credential scanning only arrived with this initialization - the .git/hooks/pre-commit hook did not exist before and was written by devctl scaffold in this run. The more material exposure is unreviewed: these scripts kill processes by port and by name and force-remove directories (kill-port.ps1, kill-worktree-agents.ps1, nuke-worktrees.ps1, force-remove-dir.ps1), all running against paths supplied by project config. This failure class has already fired once in this repo's own history - PR #4, 'never name-kill node in the build protocol (it kills Claude Code itself)'. The missing work is a blast-radius review of the destructive utilities, not more secret scanning.

children.title: Extend Reliability & Resilience
children.why: Genuinely strong for a project this size: restore-session.ps1 plus psmux-dispatch -Continue recover a crashed session with its prior conversation, check-worktree-health.ps1 and check-headless-workers.ps1 detect dead or hung workers, and GIT_REDIRECT_STDERR is assigned once centrally in the shared lib to kill an entire class of dispatch abort. The gap is that recovery is entirely operator-initiated - every one of these is a command a person runs after noticing something is wrong. Nothing detects a failed worker and acts. Worker startup failure is a known standing pain point on this project.

children.title: Extend Observability
children.why: poll-worktrees.sh with poll-format.js and orchestrator-hook.sh give a live view of what every worker is doing, which is the highest-value observability for this product and it works. The limit is that it is strictly point-in-time polling: no run is recorded, so once a worker dies there is no history of what it was doing, and diagnosing a failed overnight crew depends on psmux scrollback still existing. There is no artifact you can read the morning after.

children.title: Extend Environments, CI/CD & Delivery
children.why: The highest-value gap in the repository. 126 Pester tests exist and all 126 pass, but nothing runs them: before this initialization there was no .github/workflows directory at all, and the only workflow present now is the project-automation.yml this run just scaffolded. Every one of the eight merged PRs therefore landed with no automated verification, and the suite protects only the person who remembers to invoke Invoke-Pester by hand. The tests are already written - the delivery step that would make them binding is the missing piece.

children.title: Extend Testing & Quality Architecture
children.why: Content is better than typical for a plugin repo and notably well-targeted: 126 tests across five files covering brief generation, config resolution, dispatch script invocation, slug derivation and worker-CLI profiles - which is to say, regression tests written after real failures rather than coverage theatre. Two gaps: no coverage measurement of any kind, and the suite has no automated trigger (see S43). Strong test content, absent test enforcement.

children.title: Extend Releases & Versioning
children.why: Three sources of truth for one version number and they disagree. CHANGELOG.md documents releases up to 0.4.2 dated 2026-06-23 in disciplined Keep-a-Changelog form across eight or more entries; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json declares version 0.2.2; and the plugin's own plugin.json declares no version field at all. marketplace.json is the one users actually resolve through `/plugin install crew@claude-crew`, so an installer is offered 0.2.2 of a codebase whose changelog calls itself 0.4.2 - two minor versions of documented work that installs cannot see. The changelog discipline is real; the release step that carries a bump into the two manifests does not exist.
